card: Fixes a false-positive test assertion in mining_prioritisetransaction.py where mocktime increments masked whether getblocktemplate was actually invalidated by prioritisetransaction. The test previously compared whole block template dictionaries, which always differed due to the updated curtime timestamp. The PR instead verifies that the deprioritised transaction is dropped from the new template, restoring test coverage for the mempool change introduced in #10196.
evidence: "If you remove the counter bump in CTxMemPool::PrioritiseTransaction (the fix this check was added for in #10196), the test from master still passes but this one fails." (PR description)
problem: A functional test designed to verify that PrioritiseTransaction invalidates the cached block template always passed trivially. Advancing mocktime changed the template's curtime property, masking whether the template was actually regenerated or the deprioritised transaction was omitted.

risk.why: Only functional test code is modified, with no impact on production consensus or node behavior.

scope_notes: Small test-only assertion change (+7/-5 in one Python test).
summary: Fixes a test assertion in mining_prioritisetransaction.py to ensure getblocktemplate rebuilds block templates as expected after calling prioritisetransaction. Instead of comparing whole templates whose curtime field always changes after advancing mocktime, the test now checks that the deprioritised transaction is dropped from the returned template.
